title: A Trail for the Summit
premise: Desert ranger Beatrix Dunmore has spent five years erasing herself from every record, tracking a thief who stole the only proof of her old identity. When a dying prospector trades her a map to a forbidden river source for a promise to deliver it, Beatrix inherits more than paper: the map is the same one her father died carrying, and the thief she hunts wants it too. Forced into an uneasy alliance with the thief, Wren, Beatrix follows the river upstream through canyon country where a mining syndicate kills to keep the source secret. At the summit spring, Beatrix must choose between exposing the truth that would restore her name and protecting Wren, whose testimony could destroy them both; she burns the map, testifies anyway, and finally stops measuring life in miles.
about_author: Emrys Voss is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade running expeditions through the American Southwest before turning to fiction. Their work explores how landscapes reshape the people who try to lose themselves in them.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Establishes her solitary ranger life in the Redwash desert and her ritual of measuring time in distance traveled. She nearly catches the thief who stole her identity papers five years ago, but he slips away again. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like armor.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Beatrix finds prospector Elias Crane gut-shot by a dry wash. He trades her a waterproofed map to the Silverhead River's source for a promise: carry it to the summit or burn it, never sell it. He dies naming a name she recognizes—her father's. Beat: grief rekindled.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Studying the map at night, she realizes the route matches fragments of her father's last expedition and that the syndicate stamp on its border means someone killed for it. She decides to follow the river upstream. Beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Thief in the Waterhole
chapters.summary: Wren's POV introduces the thief: he stole Beatrix's papers not to sell but because they contain a forged signature linking him to the syndicate's payrolls. He's been shadowing her, knowing the map will draw out his old employers. Beat: guilt and calculation.

chapters.title: Ambush at Split Rock
chapters.summary: Syndicate riders ambush Beatrix at Split Rock. Wren intervenes unexpectedly, saving her life, and she captures him rather than thank him. Under threat of leaving him tied for the vultures, he offers the truth about her father. Beat: reluctant alliance forged under duress.

chapters.title: Terms of Travel
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They negotiate an uneasy truce: Wren leads through syndicate territory, Beatrix keeps the map. Flashbacks reveal her father's expedition and Wren's years as the syndicate's courier. Beat: wary trust, each hiding a piece of the truth.

chapters.title: Downstream Town
chapters.summary: They resupply in Meridian Flats, a company town where the syndicate's reach is visible everywhere. Beatrix sees a wanted poster—with Wren's face and a price. A barmaid who knew her father slips Beatrix a warning: 'He didn't drown.' Beat: the past pressing closer.

chapters.title: The First Crossing
chapters.summary: Action chapter. Crossing the flooded river narrows, Wren nearly drowns; Beatrix saves him against her own judgment. In the aftermath he admits he was on her father's final crew—and ran when the shooting started. Beat: shame confessed, contempt beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Canyon of Echoes
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In a slot canyon, they find her father's camp, five years frozen: a journal page proving he found contamination at the source, not treasure. The syndicate didn't kill him for gold—they killed him for what he knew. Beat: rage and revelation.

chapters.title: Riders Behind
chapters.summary: Syndicate trackers close in. A two-day chase through badlands ends with their horses lost and the pair on foot. Wren takes a bullet graze shielding Beatrix. Beat: loyalty tested by fire; she begins to see him as more than a thief.

chapters.title: Night Without Fire
chapters.summary: Quiet character chapter, dual POV around a cold camp. Wren explains why he never sold her papers: reading them, he understood what it cost to be erased, as he once was. Beatrix admits she stopped going home because home stopped existing. Beat: intimacy without touch.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: The only crossing into high country is syndicate-controlled. They bluff through using Wren's old courier credentials, but the bridge captain recognizes him and lets them pass only to follow. Beat: dread—the trap is already sprung.

chapters.title: Betrayal's Shape
chapters.summary: Beatrix discovers Wren sent a signal from the bridge—a message meant to lure the syndicate's director, Voss-Hale, away from the source so evidence can be taken downstream. Or so he claims. Trust fractures. Beat: suspicion poisoning everything.

chapters.title: Alone Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: Beatrix strikes out alone at dawn, leaving Wren bound. High-altitude chapters of endurance: storm, thin air, doubt. She rereads her father's journal and understands his promise to her mother—to come back clean, not rich. Beat: solitude stripping her to essentials.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Beatrix reaches the summit spring: not gold, but a poisoned watershed the syndicate has been secretly contaminating with tailings for years, sickening every town downstream. Her father found it first. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Voss-Hale Arrives
chapters.summary: Climax begins. The director's party reaches the source—Wren escaped and led them here deliberately, trading himself to buy Beatrix time to document the site. She watches from the rocks as Wren is interrogated and refuses to give her up. Beat: sacrifice witnessed.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Burns
chapters.summary: She has the map, the journal, water samples, photographs. Burning the map destroys the syndicate's claim to secrecy—but also her father's last legacy. She feeds it to the wind and keeps the truth instead. Beat: choosing truth over possession.

chapters.title: The Descent Fight
chapters.summary: Climax action. Beatrix descends into the syndicate camp at night, frees Wren, and they fight through the gorge as the storm breaks. Voss-Hale falls to his death reaching for the burning map's ashes. Beat: survival at its steepest price.

chapters.title: Downstream Testimony
chapters.summary: Resolution begins. In Meridian Flats, Beatrix gives sworn testimony, surrendering her anonymity and her stolen-name safety forever. Wren corroborates, accepting prosecution for his courier years. Beat: courage as exposure, not concealment.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: The verdicts land: the syndicate collapses, Wren serves a reduced term, Beatrix is cleared but no longer invisible—her name in every paper. She visits her father's grave for the first time in five years. Beat: grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: The Thief's Release
chapters.summary: A year later, Beatrix meets Wren at the prison gate. Neither knows how to be people rather than fugitives. He asks if she still measures in miles. She says she's learning to measure in seasons instead. Beat: tender, uncertain hope.

chapters.title: A Trail for the Summit
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Beatrix's POV. She leads a small survey team back up the river—not fleeing, but guiding—as restoration of the watershed begins. At the summit spring she leaves her father's compass and walks down unburdened. Beat: belonging earned, the trail finally walked whole.
